topic.title: Exploration Complexity and Regret in Reinforcement Learning
topic.overview: This topic studies how much interaction a reinforcement-learning agent needs to learn effective behavior. Papers derive sample-complexity and regret guarantees under different observations, reward information, state representations, and constraints. Reward-free exploration is a useful example: an agent first collects information about dynamics, then must solve tasks whose rewards are revealed later.
topic.whyItMatters: Theoretical bounds identify the information that learning fundamentally requires and whether an algorithm uses it efficiently. Constraint guarantees also distinguish genuinely controlled behavior from performance metrics that allow violations at different times to cancel out.
topic.evolution: The representatives range from mistake bounds and policy-search complexity to optimal exploration and structured function approximation. Recent work addresses trajectory feedback, action-triggered observations, and strong regret in constrained problems. The strength of these guarantees changes with feasibility assumptions and the available feedback.
openQuestions: How can exploration remain reusable across many future rewards?
Which optimal interaction guarantees can be retained with computationally practical function approximation?

papers.tldr: PANDA optimizes hierarchical reinforcement learning problems with competing lower-level policies using first-order updates and provable convergence to stationary points.

papers.title: Data- and Variance-dependent Regret Bounds for Online Tabular MDPs
papers.tldr: For tabular MDPs with known transitions, new algorithms achieve regret bounds that adapt to data complexity and stochastic variance.

papers.title: Efficiently Solving Discounted MDPs via Predictions with Unknown Prediction Errors
papers.tldr: Transition predictions can improve discounted-MDP sample efficiency in favorable cases without known prediction accuracy, despite a worst-case impossibility bound.

papers.title: Exact Unlearning in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper constructs stable tabular RL algorithms that support exact user-data deletion with quantified computational and regret trade-offs.

papers.title: Fast Non-Episodic Finite-Horizon RL with K-Step Lookahead Thresholding
papers.tldr: A tabular reinforcement-learning method combines K-step planning with time-varying action thresholds and adaptively deepens lookahead during evaluation.

papers.title: From Generative to Episodic: Sample-Efficient Replicable Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: For low-horizon tabular problems, a new replicable RL algorithm nearly closes the sample-efficiency gap between generative access and episodic exploration.

papers.title: Improved Bounds for Reward-Agnostic and Reward-Free Exploration
papers.tldr: The paper broadens an efficient reward-agnostic exploration guarantee and closes the known bounds gap for reward-free exploration.

papers.title: Minimax-Optimal Policy Regret in Partially Observable Markov Games
papers.tldr: An epoch-based optimistic algorithm achieves near-matching upper and lower policy-regret rates in partially observable games with adaptive opponents.

papers.title: Minimax Optimal Strategy for Delayed Observations in Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: An augmentation-and-confidence algorithm achieves minimax-optimal regret up to logarithmic factors for tabular reinforcement learning with delayed states.

papers.title: Model-Free Robust Average-Reward Reinforcement Learning with Sample Complexity Analysis
papers.tldr: Robust Halpern Iteration provides model-free robust average-reward learning with finite sample guarantees under a generative-model sampling setup.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Regret for Policy Optimization in Contextual MDPs with General Offline Function Approximation
papers.tldr: OPO-CMDP provides a high-probability regret bound with optimal state and action dependence for contextual sequential decision problems.

papers.title: Post-Training with Policy Gradients: Optimality and the Base Model Barrier
papers.tldr: For linear autoregressive models under a margin condition, policy gradients are nearly optimal but outcome rewards can face an exponential base-model barrier.

papers.title: Posterior Sampling Reinforcement Learning with Gaussian Processes for Continuous Control: Sublinear Regret Bounds for Unbounded State Spaces
papers.tldr: A high-probability bound on visited states enables sharper Bayesian regret guarantees for Gaussian-process posterior sampling in unbounded state spaces.

papers.title: Rate or Fate? RLV$^\varepsilon$R: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Noisy Rewards
papers.tldr: In the paper's model, verifier noise slows learning when true positives exceed false positives and reverses learning when the inequality flips.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Reachability: Guaranteeing Asymptotic Optimality
papers.tldr: Iteratively refining unknown environment parameters connects finite-time approximate reachability guarantees to exact optimality in the limit.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning with Action-Triggered Observations
papers.tldr: For action-dependent intermittent observations, a structured reinforcement-learning algorithm matches the known regret rate for fully observable linear MDPs.

papers.title: Rethinking the Hardness of PbRL: A Provable General Regret Bound
papers.tldr: RTPQ achieves a square-root regret guarantee for preference-based reinforcement learning under broad function approximation, with a new measure of problem difficulty.

papers.title: Towards Achieving Optimal Strong Regret and Constraint Violation via Computationally Efficient Model-free RL
papers.tldr: APMPO provides sublinear strong regret and constraint-violation guarantees, with near-optimal rates under strict feasibility and weaker rates without it.
